title: Every facade query is a parameterised prepared statement
asA: developer who needs the persistence boundary to leave no SQL-injection surface for consumer arguments
iWant: every facade query to be a static SQL literal issued via `db.prepare(...).bind(...)`, with no string-concatenated SQL and no `exec(<consumer string>)` on any path
soThat: consumer arguments never traverse the SQL parser and the vendor's parameter-binding layer is the only place values reach the engine

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every call site in the facade module that reaches the D1 binding is a `db.prepare(<static SQL literal>).bind(...)` chain terminating in `.first()`, `.all()`, `.run()`, or `.raw()`. No call site inside the facade calls `db.exec(...)` with any string other than a static SQL literal authored inside the facade module.
acceptanceCriteria.when: every call to the D1 binding is inspected for its SQL argument shape
acceptanceCriteria.then: every `prepare` argument is a static string literal (not a template with an interpolation for a value, not a `+`-concatenation with any consumer argument, not a function-returned string) and no `exec` call takes a non-literal string; a targeted grep for `\.exec(`, `\.prepare(` template-literal interpolations, and `\+` inside prepared-statement arguments returns only the known-safe literal-static occurrences the facade documents

acceptanceCriteria.description: The facade does not export a general-purpose query method whose parameter is a SQL string supplied by a consumer.
acceptanceCriteria.then: no exported function's typed parameter list includes a SQL-string parameter (a parameter named `sql`, `query`, `statement`, or typed as an arbitrary string that reaches `db.prepare` or `db.exec` inside the facade body); the boundary refuses raw-query passthrough by construction

acceptanceCriteria.description: A facade verb invoked with a value containing SQL metacharacters (a semicolon, a comment marker, an OR-1=1 fragment, a quote) treats the value as a bound parameter, not as SQL syntax: the resulting query behaves as if the value were the literal string.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a facade verb that accepts a string argument (a lookup by name, an insert of a title, an update by identifier) and a probe value containing the literal characters `'; DROP TABLE domainTable; --`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the verb is invoked with the probe value against a local D1 database
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invocation completes without side-effect against tables other than the one the verb legitimately touches, and a follow-up `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM domainTable` returns the same count as before the invocation (no DROP), and the probe value round-trips as an ordinary string wherever the verb persisted or returned it
